ideas.inspiration: Nothing adds one handcrafted, unique, endgame-difficulty dungeon per biome. Idea: a named legendary dungeon per biome, placed exactly once per world, with multiple floors and key/lock progression, mini-bosses and a final guardian. Endgame difficulty regardless of biome, unique loot tied to Crafting, optional reset. Borrow warpalicious' asset-bundle and Jotunn room pipeline, EWD's dungeon YAML and Dungeon Splitter's instancing. Avoid procedural sameness. The most art-heavy idea: it needs a Unity asset pipeline.

ideas.name: Spyglass
ideas.description: See things far away
ideas.sketch: While a key/secondary action is held (spyglass equipped or in inventory), force first person (m_distance=0), call SetTempFOV(65/zoom) and scale mouse sensitivity, show a vignette and a long raycast readout (name/distance of target). Optional: drop a map pin or reveal a small fog radius at the hit point via Minimap.AddPin / private Minimap.Explore.
ideas.risks: Objects beyond the synced simulation distance do not exist (only terrain/LOD visible); GrapplingPoint shares the temp-FOV API; camera/first-person mods fight over m_distance/FOV; held-item version needs a model/icon and is deleted from inventories without the mod.

existingMods.name: Spyglass (Advize)
existingMods.notes: Craftable and upgradable; 3 zoom levels (right mouse / Shift+right mouse, gamepad); also a bash weapon that can block; ServerSync.

existingMods.name: Monocular (jg224)
existingMods.notes: Handheld monocular with mouse-wheel zoom.

existingMods.name: Visby Lens (Nexus 432)
existingMods.notes: Lore-friendly spyglass with right-click zoom.

ideas.inspiration: The user thought this did not exist, but basic zoom (a GameCamera.m_fov change) is solved and maintained. Only worth building as an exploration tool: reveal the map in the view cone at long range (ties to cartography), one-key pin on the target, show the target's name, stars, variant and kill count (kill count / mob variant / Compendium), sky-pointed weather forecast, and ship crow's-nest use. Smooth zoom, vignette, sway. Advize is GPL, so reimplement rather than copy.

ideas.name: Swim dive
ideas.description: Allows to dive vertically
ideas.sketch: Postfix Character.UpdateSwimming for the local player to override vertical velocity from Crouch (dive) / Jump (ascend) read directly from ZInput, letting buoyancy return the player when released; track head under water via GetHeadPoint vs GetLiquidLevel to drain a breath meter and apply Drowning damage. Remove the camera water clamp while submerged and apply an underwater fog/tint.
ideas.risks: Water volume trigger may not contain the player at depth (OnTriggerExit sets level -10000 -> falling); ocean surface may be invisible from below and no vanilla underwater effect; needs dive animation for good visuals; other clients see an upright sinking swimmer unless they run the mod; Ashlands water/tar differ.
relatedIdeas: New ability depending on skill level

existingMods.name: BetterDiving (MainStreetGaming)
existingMods.notes: Crouch toggles diving and you dive where you look; Diving skill; oxygen bar; fast swim. Fork of Easy_Develope's Valheim Diving Mod (Nexus 1271).

existingMods.name: VikingsDoSwim (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: Swim speed and stamina scale with the Swim skill, plus diving. Incompatible with BetterDiving.

existingMods.name: Dive In (sighsorry)
existingMods.notes: Dedicated ascend/descend keys (true vertical diving), depth-scaled stamina drain, underwater visuals, creatures chase underwater, weapons usable in water.

existingMods.name: Underwater (Crystal) / UnderTheSea (Jacobo)
existingMods.notes: Walk on the seafloor; crouch to dive.

ideas.inspiration: Vanilla keeps the player at the surface (Character.m_swimDepth = 2) and has no breath system. Diving is covered three times over, by mutually incompatible mods that patch the same swimming code. Only build our own as the base for the Underwater biome: vertical dive keys, Breath tied to the vanilla Swim skill, crafted diving gear (helmet, weights, underwater lantern), cold/pressure in Deep North waters. Or soft-depend on BetterDiving (Apache-2.0) and ship only content.

ideas.name: Hip lantern as utility item
ideas.sketch: Clone the vanilla Lantern item, set m_itemType = Utility, and add an attach_Hips (or thigh bone) child holding the lantern visual + Light under an offset holder, since AttachArmor zeroes the attach child's local transform; copy durability settings and reduce light range, add a recipe.
ideas.risks: Uses the single utility slot (competes with Megingjord/Wishbone/Wisplight); an extra slot would conflict with ExtraSlots/AzuEPI-style mods; clients without the prefab see nothing; items deleted if mod removed; many lights cost performance (no shadows).

existingMods.name: HipLantern (shudnal)
existingMods.notes: Craftable hip lantern that burns fuel (0 = infinite), refuel recipe, own custom slot or the utility slot, configurable light, item-stand placement, EpicLoot integration, server-synced.

existingMods.name: ExtraSlots (shudnal)
existingMods.notes: Extra equipment slots; the usual companion to HipLantern.

ideas.inspiration: Already solved and well maintained, so do not duplicate it. Vanilla has a single utility slot (Humanoid.m_utilityItem) plus a trinket slot. If we touch lighting, make the vanilla lanterns (Dvergr and the new 1.0 lanterns) hip-mountable, or fold it into a broader 'utility belt' UX idea. Recommendation: deprioritize.

ideas.name: Distant horizon
ideas.description: See farther
ideas.sketch: Client horizon profile: enlarge TerrainLod (6-8 km, coarser vertices), raise camera far clip, scale fog density, optional LOD bias; optional server part accepts higher simulation levels (server clamps clients), and mark big landmark prefabs m_distant so they stream in the far ring. True distant objects (impostors of unloaded vegetation) would be a separate very-hard project.
ideas.risks: GPU/CPU cost and hitches from HeightmapBuilder rebuilds every 256m; network/CPU cost of higher simulation distance; depth precision; fog/sky mismatch; m_distant changes persist in ZDO flags; overlap with Render Limits-style mods and ValheimPlus graphics/camera options.

existingMods.name: Render Limits (JereKuusela)
existingMods.status: 1.15.0, 2026-08-30, deprecated (probably superseded by the vanilla 1.0 setting)
existingMods.notes: Number of active, loaded and generated zones; real-terrain distance; LOD bias; clutter distance; shadows; server caps.

existingMods.name: RenderSettings (romenh)
existingMods.notes: Extra camera and render settings.

ideas.inspiration: Vanilla 1.0 added a SimulationDistance setting (more near zones; far ring fixed at 2; server-synced). Distant terrain already draws as a low-detail heightmap (Heightmap.IsDistantLod), but objects beyond loaded zones do not. Nothing like Minecraft's 'Distant Horizons' exists for Valheim. Idea: a client-only impostor layer for trees, rocks and landmarks beyond loaded zones (from WorldGenerator and vegetation data, or cached from visited zones), plus better distant terrain and fog. Unlike Render Limits it loads nothing from the server. High technical risk: investigate Unity 6 rendering and instancing first.

ideas.name: One trinket per trophy
ideas.sketch: A data table maps each trophy to {station, mats, m_maxAdrenaline, equip SE, full-adrenaline SE}. Clone a vanilla trinket prefab, set SharedData, and generate icons by compositing the trophy icon. Register items, recipes and SEs (Jotunn). The vanilla adrenaline pop applies m_fullAdrenalineSE with no patch. Implement effects with a few parameterized SE_Stats subclasses.
ideas.risks: About 70 items to balance and create icons for. Removing the mod deletes the items. SE name-hash collisions. Overlap with trophy-buff mods. Relative balance against vanilla trinkets.

existingMods.name: ClassTrinkets (JamesJonesTV)
existingMods.notes: 40 trinkets (8 classes x 5 ranks) with static stats. Rank 1 needs a class trophy.

existingMods.name: Glorious Trinkets (Catharis)
existingMods.notes: New trinkets, capes and utility items.

existingMods.name: BetterTrinkets (Schwifty)
existingMods.notes: Makes vanilla trinkets passive, and a full adrenaline bar doubles them. A rebalance, not new trinkets.

existingMods.name: TrophyBuffs (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: 72 craftable glowing trophies that can be eaten for buffs.

ideas.inspiration: Gap: map each vanilla trophy to a themed trinket that uses the 1.0 adrenaline system (ItemType.Trinket = 24, SharedData.m_maxAdrenaline, m_fullAdrenalineSE). Data-driven table of trophy -> trinket (tier metal, status effect). Clone a vanilla trinket prefab, render the trophy mesh as a pendant, generate the icon at runtime. The recipe unlocks when the trophy is known. Balance against vanilla trinkets. Feeds from the new-trophies idea and the player trophy.

ideas.name: Underwater biome
ideas.sketch: Phase 1: ocean AltBiome sub-biome (reef/abyss) adding seabed vegetation, sea creatures and ambience with vanilla ocean-depth filters, reachable from boats. Phase 2: diving - patch swimming depth with a breath status effect, lift the camera water clamp while diving and add an underwater fog/tint post-process when the camera is below the liquid level.
ideas.risks: Adding a Heightmap.Biome value breaks BiomeHelpers switches, terrain shader, minimap and AltBiomeWorldData - use AltBiome instead; one-sided water surface, no underwater lighting; no navmesh on seabed; conflicts with diving mods patching UpdateSwimming/camera; AltBiome lists must match on all peers.

existingMods.name: RtDOcean (Soloredis)
existingMods.notes: Sea life, tameable dolphins/orcas/mermaids, sharks, sunken ships with treasure, seaweed, ocean boss Belzor, relics, crops and dishes. No diving needed; no seafloor biome.

existingMods.name: SeaAnimals (Marlthon)
existingMods.notes: 12+ marine animals spawning by depth, biome and global key; rideable orca, dolphin, crocodile and shark.

existingMods.name: Bestiary (Radamanto)
existingMods.notes: Creature pack including white sharks and whales.

existingMods.name: Expand World Data (JereKuusela)
existingMods.notes: Can define new biomes and terrain in YAML.

ideas.inspiration: Ocean content exists; a real underwater biome does not. The 1.0 AltBiome system (per-sector modifiers that add or block spawns, environments, vegetation and locations, and force environments) could host ocean sub-biomes; height changes are disabled in vanilla. Idea: a deep-ocean seafloor biome with trenches, kelp, ruins, sunken longships, bioluminescence, its own environment and music, and dive-only resources. Depends on diving and Crafting breathing gear. Borrow RtDOcean's POIs and SeaAnimals' depth-based spawning. Heavy art and rendering work.

ideas.name: Deep North revamp
ideas.description: Rework Deep north to be dormant then VERY active after the first stone is broken
ideas.sketch: Server-owned staged key (vm_dn_stage). Dormant: DN spawn entries require the key, calm env weights, no DN events. When the owner of the first 'stone' destructible sees m_onDestroyed (vanilla TriggerPersistentEventOnDestroy objects such as the BlackIce/Fimbulvinter props, or a marker component on chosen props) it sets the key: spawns unlock, DN level-up multiplier, raids and persistent blizzard events start, optional heavy snow.
ideas.risks: The exact vanilla stone objects and their event wiring must be confirmed at runtime; vanilla EnvMan IsDeepnorth(x, y) bug limits DN override envs; migration for worlds already progressed; spawn-list editors (Spawn That, Expand World, CLLC) and DN content packs touch the same data; always set the key via the server from the destructible owner to avoid softlocks.

existingMods.name: MonstrumDeepNorth (Therzie)
existingMods.notes: Pre-1.0 content for the old placeholder Deep North (creatures, locations, Forsaken bosses). Obsolete.

existingMods.name: Expand World Data (JereKuusela)
existingMods.notes: Key-conditioned spawns, events and environments per biome in YAML; can prototype dormant/active phases.

existingMods.name: Spawn That / Custom Raids (ASharpPen)
existingMods.notes: Config-driven spawners and raids with global-key conditions.

existingMods.name: World Advancement Progression (VentureValheim)
existingMods.notes: Key-based progression gating.

ideas.inspiration: Nothing like this exists. In 1.0, breaking the Malicious Ice in Mörkhalla triggers a Jotun Invasion (data-driven; wiki gives prefab FimbulLocation01). Ask the user whether this is the 'first stone'. Vanilla spawns and events already gate on global keys (SpawnSystem.SpawnData.m_requiredGlobalKey, CreatureSpawner.m_requiredGlobalKey, RandomEvent.m_requiredGlobalKeys), and AltBiome can swap environments and spawn lists. Design: dormant Deep North (calm weather, sparse life) until a world key is set on the first break, then an active phase (blizzards, Jotun patrols, raids on bases in the biome, new music, more loot). Mostly data plus a small plugin; prototype with EWD or Spawn That.

ideas.name: Mob variant
ideas.description: from valheim magic (elemental, blood, etc)
ideas.sketch: The spawning client rolls a variant (fire/frost/lightning/poison/spirit/blood) from a biome/star weighted table and stores it in the creature ZDO; every peer applies tint/VFX/name from the ZDO in Character.Awake, the owner applies resistances (GetDamageModifiers), extra elemental damage/status effects (Attack.ModifyDamage), death effects and variant essence drops for the magic/crafting mods.
ideas.risks: Direct overlap with CLLC infusions/effects and EpicLoot damage modifiers; inheritance on taming/procreation; exclude bosses; particle cost per creature; spawns happen on clients so the mod must be everywhere.

existingMods.name: StarLevelSystem (MidnightMods)
existingMods.notes: Fire, Frost, Poison, Lightning and Elemental Chaos modifiers plus novas, EitrDrain, Splitter; per-level colors and sizes; YAML loot; API. Incompatible with CLLC.

existingMods.name: EliteCreaturesReborn (MilkyTeam)
existingMods.notes: 13 mutations (Leeching, Warding, Bloated, Splintering, Blinking, Gilded...), colored nameplates, per-biome YAML, 4 loot modes.

existingMods.name: Monster Modifiers (warpalicious)
existingMods.notes: 31 modifiers, one per star; open source (jneb802/MonsterModifiers).

existingMods.name: CreatureLevelAndLootControl (Smoothbrain)
existingMods.notes: Original Fire/Frost/Lightning/Spirit/Poison/Chaos infusions.

ideas.inspiration: Generic affixes are well covered. Variants themed on Valheim's magic schools are not. Elemental-touched variants: fire, frost or lightning auras mirroring the vanilla staffs. Blood-cursed variants: lifesteal, raising skeletons, sacrifice-HP bursts. Give each distinct shaders and drop essences or reagents for the Magic/Crafting revamps. Regional variants via AltBiome sectors (e.g. a Blood-soaked Swamp). Be additive to, or plug into, the StarLevelSystem API rather than compete with its install base.

ideas.name: Trophy on mobs without trophy
ideas.sketch: At ZNetScene.Awake, scan prefabs with a CharacterDrop that has no ItemType.Trophy drop, and append a Drop for a new trophy (cloned trophy prefab with a swapped mesh/icon, free m_trophyPos, <name>_lore localization, and an 'attach' child for item stands). Use a configurable chance and exclusions (summons, tames).
ideas.risks: Drop-table mods (Drop That, CLLC, EpicLoot) may overwrite m_drops, so ordering matters. Pseudo-random smoothing for chances <= 0.3. Trophy panel overlap. Needs art per creature.

existingMods.name: Drop That (ASharpPen)
existingMods.notes: Loot-table configurator. Can add existing items as drops, not new trophies. We must coexist because it rewrites CharacterDrop.

existingMods.name: CreatureLevelAndLootControl (Smoothbrain)
existingMods.notes: Level and loot control. No new trophy items.

existingMods.name: TrophyBuffs (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: Craftable decorative trophies, not creature drops.

ideas.inspiration: Clear gap. The wiki lists creatures with no trophy: Greyling, Gull, Crow, Root, Fish, Leviathan, Oozer, Bat, Chicken/Hen, Seeker Brood, Ash Crow, Charred Twitcher, Skugg. Plan: clone a trophy prefab with a head mesh taken from the creature's renderer and a runtime icon. Inject a low-rate CharacterDrop entry. Register it as a trophy so Player.AddTrophy and the trophy wall work. Give each one a use (trinkets, item stands). Fish (items) and Leviathan (a location) need special handling.

ideas.name: Hunting
ideas.description: shows gatherables and animals nearby on the minimap (capped to the discovery radius at 100)
ideas.sketch: A client tracker runs every 0.5-1 s. It collects loaded non-player characters and available pickables within min(config radius, m_exploreRadius) and keeps one pooled non-saved PinData per object, updating m_pos. The icon is replaced with the item icon (ItemData.GetIcon) or the creature's trophy icon. Pins are removed when out of range or picked. Optionally gate behind a Hunting SE, trinket or skill.
ideas.risks: Pin churn and performance in dense areas: pool pins and cap counts. Only loaded objects are visible. Pin-manager mods (Pinnacle, AutoMapPins) may treat these pins oddly: use save:false and a distinct type. Offer a server-synced disable flag for 'cheat' concerns.

existingMods.name: OneMapToRuleThemAll (DrummerCraig)
existingMods.notes: Shared map plus a client radar. Nearby objects and creatures show as temporary pins that fade, and creatures are tracked live.

existingMods.name: Hunting (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: Hunting skill (XP from bow, knife and spear) with a configurable auto-track radius for prey, and yield scaling. The closest to the progression framing.

existingMods.name: CreatureTrackerMinimap (Fusionette)
existingMods.notes: All creatures on the minimap using their trophy sprite as the icon, with a drop-icon fallback. Open source.

existingMods.name: UnderTheRadar (Kits_Bitz)
existingMods.notes: Former reference: live pins for pickables, ores, critters and locations within a radius.

ideas.inspiration: The radar/ESP exists. Earned hunter craft does not. Plan: the radius grows with a Hunting skill or a trinket up to Minimap.m_exploreRadius (100). Active only while crouched, or with a horn or tracking potion. Separate toggles for animals and pickables. Fading, non-saved pins (Minimap.AddPin with save=false), trophy icons. Throttle scans to about 1 Hz over Character.GetAllCharacters and a cached list of Pickable objects. Client-only.

ideas.name: Sap collector on other trees
ideas.description: Get new cooking / crafting item
ideas.sketch: Clone piece_sapcollector into a tree tap. Replace the root requirement with an UpdatePlacementGhost rule requiring a TreeBase within 0.3 m. Use a custom TreeTap component copying the s_lastTime/s_product/s_level accumulation and mapping tree prefab to output item (birch syrup, resin, oak tannin, ember sap). Do not attach ResourceRoot to every tree.
ideas.risks: New items need icons. Uninstalling leaves unknown prefabs. Chopping the tree breaks the connection. Balance against vanilla Sap. Adding ResourceRoot to all trees would add thousands of timers.
relatedIdeas: Ashlands trees (safe in shield, crops burn out, trees scorched outside)

existingMods.name: ResinCollector (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: A build piece that works only on trees (Meadows, Black Forest, Plains) and collects resin. Configurable and server-synced. Proves it is feasible.

existingMods.name: BetterSapCollector (xtavim)
existingMods.notes: Tunes the vanilla sap collector and ancient-root speeds and capacities. Open source.

ideas.inspiration: The vanilla SapCollector needs a ResourceRoot parent (level and regen in the ZDO), and only Mistlands Ancient Roots have one. Plan: a ResourceRoot-like component or a 'Tap' piece that finds a TreeBase, with a new output per species. Examples: birch syrup (cooking), pine pitch (tar alternative), oak tannin (leather), Yggdrasil or Ashwood reagents (magic). Add a drain cost so it is not free. A cross-category chain: gather -> cook -> craft.

ideas.name: Better fishing
ideas.description: It suck, pick another minigame
ideas.sketch: Keep the vanilla cast, bait and bite logic. Once hooked, show a tension or zone-tracking UI whose difficulty comes from fish quality, bait and skill. A FishingFloat.FixedUpdate prefix skips the block-to-reel branch and drives line length from minigame progress. Success reproduces the vanilla path (Catch, SetCatch(null), OnHooked(null), destroy the float); failure loses the fish.
ideas.risks: Private members need AccessTools. Input must not trigger attack or block, which cancels the float. A prototype can use procedural UGUI, but polish needs sprites. Conflicts with other fishing mods patching the same FixedUpdate.

existingMods.name: PeasFishing (Laki)
existingMods.notes: The only minigame replacement: a Stardew-style vertical catch bar (hold or release Shift), a fish-nearby HUD and a clock. Client-only.

existingMods.name: Reely SpecTackleLure (Neobotics)
existingMods.notes: Gear: craftable and upgradable rods, bait, field skinning, deep-sea danger. No minigame.

existingMods.name: FishTrap (Qmds)
existingMods.notes: Passive baited traps in four tiers.

existingMods.name: TheFisher (Marlthon)
existingMods.notes: More than 30 new fish and aquariums (content).

ideas.inspiration: A Stardew clone exists. A Valheim-native minigame does not. Idea: line tension and rod bend. The fish pulls and you steer against it, reeling raises tension, stamina drains, and rod quality and skill widen the safe band. Species get behavior profiles. Keep the vanilla FishingFloat bite phase and replace only the reel phase. Support gamepad and hold/toggle. Pair with passive traps and gear for progression.

ideas.name: Weather staff
ideas.description: Change the weather with the staff
ideas.sketch: Casting spawns a networked weather totem whose ZDO stores env name, radius and expiry; each client's EnvMan.GetEnvironmentOverride postfix returns that env while the local player is inside an active totem (below boss/raid overrides). Variants or a radial menu pick Clear/Rain/Storm/Fog/Snow from EnvMan.m_environments filtered per biome; optional wind control.
ideas.risks: Override priority vs raid/boss/AltBiome/persistent-event envs and forced EnvZones; clients without the mod see vanilla weather (wet/cold and env-gated spawns desync); balance (sailing wind exploits, mist is biome-gated ParticleMist); conflicts with other EnvMan-patching mods.

existingMods.name: WeatherStones (GoldenJude)
existingMods.notes: Craftable menhir: type a weather name to force it in a radius. Closest concept, but dead.

existingMods.name: Rune Magic (hyleanlegend)
existingMods.notes: Runes learned from Runestones: Canopy (blocks rain locally), Calm Waters, Dry Land, Ocean Currents... Lore-friendly.

existingMods.name: Seasons (shudnal)
existingMods.notes: Seasonal weather weights, frozen water; a reference for environment control.

existingMods.name: WeatherTool (Nexus 371) / WeatherTweaks (Alastor)
existingMods.notes: Console env commands and weather weights.

ideas.inspiration: Vanilla already has EnvMan.SetForceEnvironment, EnvMan.m_debugEnv and EnvZone.m_force. Idea: an Elemental Magic staff that, when channeled, casts Clear Skies, Call Storm or Summon Fog for N minutes. Costs eitr plus a reagent, has a cooldown, and its duration and radius scale with skill. The server owns the forced environment. Synergies: clear weather for sailing, storms that boost lightning magic, fog for stealth. Borrow Rune Magic's lore framing; avoid WeatherStones' type-a-string UI.

ideas.name: Ritual
ideas.description: (consuming items, requiring multiple people)
ideas.sketch: Build a custom altar piece with a ZNetView component. Players join via Interact; the owner stores participant IDs and join times in the ZDO. Players offer items: the owner validates, increments ZDO counters and replies with a confirmation RPC so the offering client removes the items (OfferingBowl/Feast pattern). Once N participants stay within the radius for the channel duration, the owner resolves: SEs by hash to participants, a boss or event spawn, or a reward drop.
ideas.risks: Ownership can change mid-ritual, so all state must live in the ZDO. Item dupes are possible if removal is not confirmed. Version mismatches between players. Needs assets (altar, VFX). Overlaps with Crafting and Building design.
relatedIdeas: New magical items based on valheim magic (ward, heal)

existingMods.name: Krumpac Sacrificing Altars
existingMods.notes: God altars, a praying skill, sacrifices for blessings. Single player.

existingMods.name: CustomizeAltars (Huntardys)
existingMods.notes: JSON config for boss altar items and spawns.

existingMods.name: Vikings Summoner (Radamanto)
existingMods.notes: Ritual artifacts and summoning totems are flavour only; one player uses an item.

existingMods.name: RtDMonsters (Soloredis)
existingMods.notes: Summon custom bosses through altar items.

ideas.inspiration: No mod requires several participants. Vanilla building blocks: OfferingBowl (consume items, spawn), Incinerator (consume, produce), ShieldGenerator and PrivateArea (area effects). Ours: a ritual circle with N runestones that players must interact with at the same time, synchronized through the ZDO. It consumes offerings and triggers summons, weather, area buffs, crop growth or a raid. A strong co-op hook and a cross-category magic theme.

ideas.name: New summons
ideas.sketch: Clone the Dead Raiser setup (a staff whose attack projectile is a SpawnAbility, plus Skeleton_Friendly with Tameable as a summon) and swap in cloned or new creatures. Configure m_maxSpawned, m_levelUpSettings (Blood Magic tiers), m_copySkill, m_unsummonDistance and m_levelUpOwnerSkill. Give each summon a role item: a tank that taunts, or a healer using a FriendHurt AI item with a heal Aoe.
ideas.risks: m_maxSpawned counts every loaded instance, including other players' summons (use distinct prefabs or patch the count). Follow and unsummon match on player name. Performance with many summons. Conflicts with taming mods (AllTameable-style) that patch Tameable. New models and animations are needed unless cloning vanilla creatures.
relatedIdeas: New magical items based on valheim magic (ward, heal)

existingMods.name: Cheb's Necromancy (ChebGonaz)
existingMods.notes: Undead minions from wands (warriors, archers, mages, workers), commands (follow, wait, roam, teleport), utility pylons. Uses Jötunn. Unlicense source. About 119K downloads.

existingMods.name: Vikings Summoner (Radamanto)
existingMods.notes: Necromancer weapons, totems and armor per biome.

existingMods.name: MagicPlugin (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: Summoning totems (7 creatures) within a large magic content pack.

existingMods.name: Summon Mastery (Kolefield)
existingMods.notes: Summons scale with the staff's upgrade level and follow you through portals. Open source.

ideas.inspiration: Vanilla summons use SE_Spawn or spawn attacks and are short-lived tames without commands. Undead is thoroughly covered by Cheb's. Ours: nature, elemental or spirit summons that fit the lore, produced by the ritual system, with a small command layer (hold, follow, attack the pinged target) tied to the ping revamp. Borrow Cheb's commands and Summon Mastery's scaling and portal following.

ideas.name: New magical items based on valheim magic (ward, heal)
ideas.sketch: Clone StaffShield, StaffHeal or StaffBlocker. Ward: a friendly Aoe applying a custom SE_Shield variant (absorb scales with skill, optional reflect in the style of SE_React), or a placed ward totem projecting a small dome in the style of ShieldGenerator. Heal: a channelled staff (m_loopingAttack) whose friendly Aoe applies a heal-over-time SE that overrides SetLevel to scale with Blood Magic, paid with health or eitr.
ideas.risks: Vanilla already ships StaffHeal, StaffShield and StaffBlocker, so the new items must be clearly different. Custom SEs are applied by hash through hits, so they must be registered in ObjectDB on all clients. Balance vs magic content packs (Therzie Wizardry, EpicLoot).

existingMods.name: ArcaneWard (Madkatz)
existingMods.notes: Off-hand eitr wards that block using a separate eitr reserve scaling with skill, plus battlemage weapons. Built only from vanilla assets; needs Jötunn. Source: github.com/Torvios/ArcaneWards.

existingMods.name: Wizardry (Therzie)
existingMods.notes: Large asset pack: elemental and blood staffs, mage armor, scrolls, potions, summons, stations. About 509K downloads.

existingMods.name: MagicPlugin (blacks7ar)
existingMods.notes: Staff of Healing, totems, accessories with their own slots.

existingMods.name: RtDMagic (Soloredis)
existingMods.notes: Four tiers of AoE healing staffs.

ideas.inspiration: Extend what vanilla already has: SE_Shield (Staff of Protection), the PrivateArea ward and the Ashlands ShieldGenerator dome. Ours, ArcaneWard-style (vanilla assets and mechanics first): ward and heal totems that pulse SE_Shield or heal-over-time to allies, a personal ward charm, cleansing effects, themed through rituals rather than yet another staff pack.

ideas.name: Magic applied to non combat (craft, farming, cooking, sailing, etc,)
ideas.sketch: A shared 'blessing' framework: staffs, meads or runes grant SEs that either modify skills (craft bonus/speed, harvest radius, fishing; no patch needed) or set custom StatusAttribute bits synced via s_seAttrib. Owners of plants, stations and ships poll nearby players for those bits (cached) and apply multipliers. Station-bound runes write ZDO flags on nearby stations.
ideas.risks: Effects on world objects must run on the object's owner, so everyone needs the mod. Cost of range scans (cache them). Bit collisions with other mods. Balance. Scope: build it as a library reused by several category mods.

existingMods.name: Rune Magic (hyleanlegend)

ideas.name: New ability depending on skill level
hooks: SE_Stats (m_fallDamageModifier, m_maxMaxFallSpeed, m_jumpModifier, m_swimSpeedModifier, m_stealthModifier, m_noiseModifier, stamina-use modifiers)
ideas.sketch: Each skill gets four named abilities, at 25, 50, 75 and 100. A registry declares them as (SkillType, tier, id, name, description, passive or active); injected custom skills such as Sailing register the same way. The local player's tiers are re-evaluated on Player.OnSpawned, in a Skills.RaiseSkill postfix and on a 1 s timer (Player.Update postfix, filtered to Player.m_localPlayer). The timer also catches meads and set bonuses (SEMan.ModifySkillLevel), the console command Skills.CheatRaiseSkill and deaths, none of which go through the level-up event. Each check takes the highest tier at or below Skills.GetSkillLevel (or, as an option, the peak level kept in Player.m_customData) and compares it with a per-character cache, so a respawn does not re-announce every tier. Gained and lost abilities are announced with Player.Message and the skill icon. Passive tiers are hidden SE_Stats created at runtime (m_hidden, m_ttl 0, a unique object name because StatusEffect.NameHash hashes it). SEMan.AddStatusEffect(StatusEffect) clones them without an ObjectDB entry, and the HUD skips them. Fall damage, the fall-speed cap, jump force, swim speed, stealth, noise and stamina costs then need no Harmony patch. Passive tiers are re-added after respawn, because Player.OnDeath calls SEMan.RemoveAllStatusEffects. Active tiers reuse vanilla animation triggers that already replicate through ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger: 'jump' (Character.ForceJump) and 'dodge' (Player.UpdateDodge). Example Jump set: 25 soft landing; 50 landing roll (vanilla already queues a Dodge pressed in the air for 0.5 s and fires it after touchdown, so an UpdateGroundContact prefix only checks that queue and cuts the fall damage); 75 one jump in the air (a Player.SetControls prefix calls ForceJump); 100 slow fall while Jump is held (fall-speed cap plus a fall damage cut, because fall damage depends on the height fallen, not on speed). A SkillsDialog.Setup postfix adds each skill's four tiers to its tooltip. First pack: Run, Jump, Swim, Sneak, Dodge and Ride (24 abilities). Sailing gets its tiers from the Sailing revamp. Feasibility is medium: the framework is small and many tiers need no patch. The cost is content, and abilities that need new animation or physics (diving, ledge mantle) stay in their own ideas. Who needs it depends on the ability. Abilities on the local player are client-only: the owner simulates the player, and stealth and noise reach enemies through the player ZDO (s_stealth, s_noise). The rider owns the Sadle ZDO after Sadle.RPC_RequestControl and sends its Ride factor in the Controls RPC. Abilities on ships or on other characters need everyone.
ideas.risks: Death: on the Normal preset a hard death costs 5 % of every skill. The presets cost 1 % (Casual, Very easy), 2.5 % (Easy), 5 % (Normal) and 7.5 % (Hard), and Hardcore sets the DeathSkillsReset global key, which clears all skills through Skills.Clear (wiki). Game.m_skillReductionRate defaults to 1, so the Player prefab must override the C# initialiser Skills.m_DeathLowerFactor = 0.25; log it at runtime. A Normal death drops a tier only when the base level is less than about 5 % above it (25 to 26.3, 50 to 52.6, 75 to 78.9), but always drops the level-100 ability (100 becomes 95). Choose between current-level gating (default, vanilla-consistent) and peak-level gating. Meads and set bonuses unlock and relock tiers: avoid message spam. Skills.GetSkillLevel creates a level-0 entry for a skill the player never used, and that entry then shows in the skills panel and is saved. Only read skills listed by Skills.GetSkillList. For an injected skill without a SkillDef, that entry has m_info = null and breaks the panel and the save. Content volume: covering all 24 vanilla skills means 96 abilities. Tiers stack on vanilla's linear scaling, which needs balancing. The air jump must not fire while a grappling hook is attached, because Character.Jump uses that case to pull the hook. Conflicts: ImpactfulSkills patches Character.Jump, Character.UpdateGroundContact, Character.UpdateSwimming, Character.UpdateWalking, Player.OnSwimming and Character.AddNoise. PIXPIX Movement adds its own double jump and landing roll. GrindstoneSkills and SkillPeak also change the skills panel. Skill overhauls, XP multipliers and death-penalty settings change how fast tiers are reached or lost. Mods that clear status effects remove passive tiers until the next check. Skills are client-authoritative (saved in the character file by Skills.Save), so a server cannot enforce tiers. Ship and other-character abilities need everyone and must be evaluated on the owner.

ideas.inspiration: What to borrow: GrindstoneSkills' named milestones listed with their level in the skills panel, and its configurable milestone levels (a level above 100 turns one off). ImpactfulSkills' per-effect required levels. SkillPeak's Player.m_customData record for an optional peak-level mode. NorntasticSkillGrowth's single aggregate status effect for perk effects, the same approach as our hidden SE_Stats. PIXPIX Movement's movement actions (landing roll, double jump, dash) as candidate tiers. What existing mods get wrong: ImpactfulSkills' movement effects are hidden number increases with no unlock feedback (announcements are only on its roadmap). GrindstoneSkills skips the movement skills and must be installed on the server and every client. PIXPIX gates movement abilities on bosses, not on the skill the ability uses. NorntasticSkillGrowth adds a point-buy perk tree whose nodes are mostly unimplemented. Valheim Mastery replaces vanilla progression with its own 21 skills. What ours does differently: exactly four named abilities per vanilla skill, at 25, 50, 75 and 100. Each unlock gets one clear message, the tiers are shown in the vanilla skills tooltip, and every ability can be switched off. The first pack is client-only and covers the exploration skills (Run, Jump, Swim, Sneak, Dodge, Ride). Most passive tiers are hidden status effects rather than patches. Active tiers reuse vanilla animation triggers, and the landing roll is vanilla's own queued dodge. The Sailing revamp adds the Sailing tiers.

ideas.name: Late Game quest
ideas.description: Pick up quest from NPC to get rare items (kill specific target, bring specific item, find specific location, etc)
ideas.sketch: Client-only v1 on vanilla traders. Vanilla Trader.Interact ignores its alt argument, so Shift+E on Haldor, Hildir or the Bog Witch opens a contract board once a late-boss global key is set. The board offers 3 contracts per in-game day, seeded by ZNet.GetWorldUID + EnvMan.GetDay so every player of a world sees the same list, and keeps accepted contracts in Player.m_customData under the world UID. There are four contract types. (1) Slay a named elite: when the quester nears the pinned spot and ZoneSystem.IsZoneLoaded is true, the quester's client instantiates the creature, sets stars with Character.SetLevel, writes a name to ZDOVars.s_overrideHoverName and a contract id to a custom ZDO key, and calls BaseAI.SetPatrolPoint. Character.GetHoverName, and therefore EnemyHud, shows that name on every client, including clients without the mod. The contract completes when Game.RPC_RegisterKill arrives for that m_name while the tracked ZDO has 0 health (ZDOVars.s_health) or is destroyed (ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed). (2) Hunt N: count matching Game.RPC_RegisterKill calls (postfix) while the player is in the contract's world. Do not use the PlayerProfile per-creature totals, which cover every world. (3) Deliver: Inventory.CountItems/RemoveItem at the trader, through a Trader.UseItem prefix or a button on the board. (4) Survey: Game.DiscoverClosestLocation with discoverAll false and a chosen point (for example a random point a few km away), so the server answers with the one instance closest to that point. A Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse prefix recognises the request's unique pinName, swallows that reply and stores the position. Arrival is then a distance check or Location.GetLocation. Rewards are rare vanilla items, so only the quester needs the mod. A new NPC, custom reward items or shared party contracts would require everyone to install it (side: depends).
ideas.risks: Vanilla kill credit is keyed by player name in the victim's ZDO (set in Character.RPC_Damage, which runs on the owner). Only the owner sends it: Character.OnDeath returns before the credit loop on other peers. OnDeath is reached from CheckDeath on the owner, or from the CharacterAnimEvent.Die animation event for creatures with a death animation. The RPC carries the creature name, boss order, modifiers, attacker count and a cheat flag, but no ZDO id. So a specific target needs a second signal, players with the same name share credit, and hooks on the owner's code path (as in Haldor Fetch Quests) miss kills of creatures that another peer owns. The PlayerProfile per-creature totals cover every world the character played and also grow on cheated kills, so a 'kills since accepted' delta could be filled in another world. Spawned targets never despawn: only SpawnSystem sets the despawn-in-day and event-creature flags. An expired contract must therefore remove its tagged creature (as owner or after ZNetView.ClaimOwnership), and any player can kill it. Two questers who take the same shared daily contract would spawn two elites unless the spawn first looks for an existing tagged creature. ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed fires only on peers that hold the ZDO. With discoverAll, the server sends one reply per instance. Each reply that is not intercepted adds a pin and turns the player's view (Character.SetLookDir, when the map is closed). A prefix must not swallow the reply to a vanilla vegvisir read made at the same time, so match the pin name. The RPC only knows registered locations, and the chosen one may already be looted. The late-boss defeat keys are not in the GlobalKeys enum (it names only the first five bosses): they come from Character.m_defeatSetGlobalKey on the boss prefabs (read the prefab at runtime, or check with listkeys). Inventory counts match world level by default. EpicLoot (its own window at Haldor), HaldorBounties (a board in Haldor's shop) and TradersExtended already change the trader UI, so check that no other trader mod uses alt interact. Other risks: reward inflation, and cross-world farming if contracts are not keyed by the world UID.

ideas.inspiration: Borrow EpicLoot's world-spawned target with minions, a map pin and boss-kill gating. Borrow HaldorBounties' daily board (pick 1 of N rewards, visible reset timer), Almanac's typed objectives (Kill, Collect, ...) as the data schema, and Hildir's key-based unlocks. What existing mods get wrong: token currencies and gambling that sidestep progression (EpicLoot, Almanac); content the server admin must write in YAML or config (KG Marketplace, most of Almanac apart from its default bounties); no Ashlands or Deep North contracts (HaldorBounties stops at Mistlands, and it needs HaldorOverhaul); new NPCs that every player and the server must install (BeastMarketOutpost); owner-side kill detection that misses kills in multiplayer (Haldor Fetch Quests patches Character.RPC_Damage); and quest completion that is world-wide rather than per player (vanilla Hildir). Ours: a small, curated late-game contract board that unlocks after the Queen or a later boss. It lives on vanilla traders behind Shift+E, so StoreGui stays free for EpicLoot, TradersExtended and HaldorBounties. It has four contract types: named elite, hunt N, deliver a rare item, and survey a late-biome location. Rewards are rare vanilla items with no new currency. The client-only v1 is built only on vanilla RPCs and ZDO keys, so it works in mixed groups and on vanilla servers.

ideas.name: Smelt gold
ideas.description: We have too much gold, Smelt it in bars and create things with it (weapons, armors, tools, probably on the fancy side not necessarily strong, or with an interesting set bonus)
ideas.sketch: Treat Coins as the ore. Craft a Coin Sack (default 50 Coins) at the workbench and give it a max stack of 1, so InventoryGui.DoCrafting hands out no bonus sacks. Smelt the sack in the vanilla Smelter: append a Smelter.ItemConversion (Coin Sack to Gold Bar) to the smelter prefab's m_conversion at ZNetScene.Awake, so fuel, timing and Batch Station Feeding work unchanged. Register a Gold Bar and a small Gilded line in ObjectDB.Awake and ObjectDB.CopyOtherDB: crown, chest, legs, one weapon, a pickaxe, a trinket, and a stack or throne decor piece with comfort in the Hammer's PieceTable. Clone each one from a vanilla prefab, tint it gold, and give it a prefixed name, because vanilla 1.0 game data already uses 'Gold' for Bloodgold. Stats sit around the Bronze/Iron tier. The reason to wear the set is its bonus: a data-only SE_Stats set through m_setName, m_setSize and m_setStatusEffect. The trinket and the weapon can count toward the set (Humanoid.GetSetCount counts every slot), but the armour pieces must carry the effect, because the trinket never grants it. Optional coded perks could include better sell prices through StoreGui.SellItem (client-side). Keep m_value at 0 so nothing gold sells back to a trader, and make each upgrade level cost more bars, so the sink grows with the player's hoard. Register the prefabs once at load and keep them registered even while the feature is off. All numbers go in a server-synced config. The code is small and mostly data. Feasibility is medium rather than easy because this is the first MC mod that registers new prefabs, and every item needs a gold look and an icon.
ideas.risks: Every peer needs the mod, including the dedicated server. A peer without it loses gold items: Inventory.AddItem skips unknown prefabs when an inventory loads, and the server destroys world ZDOs it cannot instantiate (ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted). It also sees gilded armour on other players as missing (VisEquipment.SetChestEquipped logs 'Missing chest item'). As a smelter owner, it silently drops a Coin Sack that a modded client has already removed from its inventory, because Smelter.RPC_AddOre re-checks IsItemAllowed against the owner's own list. A sack that is already queued when a vanilla peer takes ownership is consumed with no output. The MC framework's Both handshake only checks the server, so a vanilla client can still join a modded server; blocking or warning those players is extra work (Jotunn's version check does it). Prefab registration must not follow the framework's live toggle: a character that loads while the prefabs are missing loses its gold items at the next save. Economy loops can duplicate coins: any m_value above 0, a melt-back recipe, or a stackable crafted intermediate (through the craft bonus). Watch for name clashes with vanilla Gold/GoldOre, Digitalroot's GoldIngot/CoinPile and Balrond's GoldBar_bal, and with display names such as vanilla's Coin Pile piece. Uninstalling the mod deletes the items. This is the first MC mod that registers prefabs, so it needs a shared helper or Jotunn. Art and balance will take most of the time.

ideas.inspiration: Digitalroot's GoldBars proves the loop works (coins, then Coin Pile, then Smelter, then Gold Ingot), but it stops at decoration: the Coin Pile crafts back into its 200 Coins, an ingot melts back into 100 Coins at the forge, and nothing uses the bars for gear. The coin-sink mods spend coins on services or on another currency rather than on things to own: RepairRequiresCoins and OttoAura (repairs, moving pieces), Weather Altar, VanillaNPC (fisherman, guards, tavern) and Ravenwood's coin exchange. Terraheim's Hyran set shows how fun a coin-themed set bonus can be. Ours would keep the vanilla Smelter step so it feels like Valheim, with a Coin Sack as the 'ore'. It would add a small hand-made Gilded line (armour, one weapon, a tool, a trinket, decor) whose value is looks plus a set bonus, not raw stats. To stay a real sink, bars and gear cannot be sold (m_value 0), the crafted intermediate gets no craft bonus, and there is no melt-back by default. Every prefab name gets a prefix (vanilla 1.0 already uses Gold for Bloodgold). Optionally, Digitalroot's GoldIngot could be accepted when that mod is installed.

ideas.name: Blood magic XP
ideas.description: Gain XP when sacrificing HP, and when any shield is HIT (not only on broken) It should also provide blood magic skill XP to the caster of the shield, not the wearer of the shield
ideas.sketch: Wrap Character.UseHealth with a prefix and postfix for the local player while Humanoid.m_currentAttack uses a Blood Magic weapon. Raise Blood Magic by the share of max HP actually lost times a config rate. Vanilla only calls UseHealth from Attack.Update and Attack.FireProjectileBurst, and paying HP gives no XP. Postfix StatusEffect.SetAttacker on SE_Shield instances to remember the caster: Character.RPC_Damage passes the caster after it adds or refreshes the bubble, and vanilla throws it away. Around SE_Shield.OnDamaged, measure what was really absorbed (the change in m_damage, capped at the remaining capacity) and keep only hits from an attacker other than the wearer. Turn that into XP in proportion to the share of the bubble's capacity used. On break (SE_Shield.IsDone prefix), give the vanilla m_levelUpSkillFactor to the caster instead of the wearer. A local caster gets the XP through Player.RaiseSkill. A remote caster gets it through a routed RPC on their Player ZNetView, sent only when their ZDO says they have the mod; otherwise vanilla rules apply and the wearer keeps the break XP. Optionally, route summon XP the same way.
ideas.risks: Besides attacker hits, the bubble absorbs every attacker-less Character.Damage hit: fall (Character.UpdateGroundContact), drowning (Player.OnSwimming), Ashlands lava and hot ocean (Character.UpdateHeatDamage), the edge of the world, and SE_Wet and SE_Stats damage ticks. A character's own AoE (Aoe.m_hitOwner) hits it with itself as the attacker. HitData.GetTotalDamage also counts chop and pickaxe damage and, in NG+, the world-level enemy bonus. So only hits from other attackers may count, with a cap per hit, per bubble and per minute. Absorb scaling with skill is unverified: the wiki says 200 + 5 per level, but the skill only reaches SetLevel when the shield Aoe keeps m_useAttackSettings, and SkeletonCrew's README says vanilla never scales it. Only eitr stops a cast-heal-recast loop. Mods that turn eitr costs into HP costs remove that limit, and recast-refill mods (BubbleBar, ShieldOverflowFix, Better Staff Of Protection) let one bubble absorb without end. The caster reference exists only in the status effect on the wearer's current owner, so a logout or respawn loses the credit, and an ownership change drops the bubble itself. Both sides need the mod: an RPC to an unmodded caster is simply lost (a ZDO-targeted one only logs 'Failed to find rpc method'), which is why the ZDO capability flag is needed to fall back to vanilla. ImpactfulSkills, SmartSkills, BloodMagicCompanion, EitrMagicExtended, SecondaryAttacks and BubbleBar patch the same methods, so detect them to avoid paying XP twice. Prefab values (the Staff_shield skill and XP factor, the shield Aoe settings, staff HP and eitr costs) must be dumped at runtime first.

ideas.inspiration: Vanilla (1.0.16): paying HP for a staff gives no XP. SE_Shield.IsDone gives m_levelUpSkillFactor XP only when damage breaks the bubble, never on expiry. That XP goes to the wearer through Skills.RaiseSkill, so a shielded tame gives nothing (Character.GetSkills returns null for non-players). The caster passed to StatusEffect.SetAttacker is thrown away. Borrow SecondaryAttacks' before/after wrapper on UseHealth: it pays for HP actually lost and respects the 1 HP floor. Borrow ImpactfulSkills' XP for absorbed damage, and BloodMagicCompanion's capability flag with a fallback to vanilla. What existing mods get wrong: ImpactfulSkills pays whoever simulates the wearer and counts fall, drowning, chop and pickaxe damage. SmartSkills records the wrong caster for shields on other players, and its expiry option (on by default) removes the break XP. BloodMagicCompanion only moves the break reward. SecondaryAttacks pays per raw HP, so more food HP levels you faster. Ours is one small mod with three rules. HP sacrifice XP scales with the share of max HP paid. Shield XP scales with the share of the bubble's capacity that other attackers' hits used up, with a cap per bubble so recast-refill mods (BubbleBar, ShieldOverflowFix) cannot farm it. All shield XP (hits and break) goes to the caster through a routed RPC, falling back to vanilla when either side lacks the mod. Optionally, it also fixes summon XP that is lost when another client simulates the summon.

ideas.name: Blood stone revamp
ideas.description: It's hard to interact with the bloodstone mechanic (+,2% damage per missing HP): provide cheap bloodmagic spell to sacrifice life / gain life on hit / lifesteal etc, to have better health management
ideas.sketch: Detect bloodstone weapons from data, not names: any weapon whose m_attack or m_secondaryAttack has m_damageMultiplierPerMissingHP or m_damageMultiplierByTotalHealthMissing above 0. That covers the seven Ashlands Bleeding weapons, probably the Deep North *Gold_BloodLightning set (prefab data, verify), and modded items. Blood rite: a hotkey, read in a Player.Update postfix for the local player, pays a share of current HP with the vanilla blood-magic rule. The rule is mirrored from Attack.GetAttackHealth (up to 33% cheaper with skill; the rite uses the Blood Magic skill factor) and from Attack.Update, which pays UseHealth(min(HP - 1, cost)) so the cost never kills. Character.UseHealth itself only clamps at 0, so the mod applies the HP - 1 cap. The rite costs no eitr, has a short cooldown, raises Blood Magic, and adds a local SE_Stats (or subclass) by reference through SEMan.AddStatusEffect. While the rite is active, a Character.Damage postfix on the attacker's client heals the local player for a share of each enemy hit. The share grows with missing HP and is capped per swing. A Hud.UpdateHealth postfix and the item tooltip show the live '+X% damage' bonus. Optional extras: the first lethal hit during the rite leaves 1 HP (prefix on Character.ApplyDamage for the local player), and a config multiplier for the per-HP bonus, applied in ObjectDB.Awake/CopyOtherDB. No new prefab, item, RPC or asset is needed. A craftable spell item instead of the hotkey would make it medium and require everyone to have the mod.
ideas.risks: Lifesteal is estimated from the outgoing hit on the attacker's client, which is also EpicLoot's approach. That happens before the victim owner applies resistances, NG+ enemy armor, difficulty scaling, the backstab bonus and the x2 on staggered targets. The outgoing total also still counts fire, poison and spirit damage that lands later as damage over time. An exact value would need an RPC back from the victim owner, and then everyone would need the mod. Multi-target swings and AoEs call Character.Damage once per target, so cap the heal per attack. Heal only on enemies. BaseAI.IsEnemy is false for tames and for every other player, so PvP needs its own IsPVPEnabled check. It is true for training dummies, and structures are not Characters. ideas.name: Cultivator revamp
ideas.description:
Base cultivator (bronze) works the same as vanilla + replant Dandelion, Rasberry bushes, Blueberry bushes, mushrooms, yellow mushrooms, Thistle need to equip the cultivator and aim at a plant bush/plant with the Replant action, it gives a new item to be planted elsewhere.
New cultivator (blackmetal) does the bronze actions + replant Cloudberries, crafted with Bronze cultivator and blackmetal ingot x5 and linnen x10
New cultivator (eitr) does the blackmetal actions + replant Yggdrasil trees, but can only grow near roots and it drains energy to grow , crafted with blackmetal cultivator and refined eitr x15
New cultivator (flametal) does the eitr actions + replant Fiddlehead and Smokepuff (can only grow in Ashlands), crafted with previous cultivator and flametal ingot x5
New cultivator (bloodgold) does the flametal actions + replant lingonberries (can only grow in Deepnorth), crafted with previous cultivator and bloodgold ingot x5
ideas.sketch: Keep one tool and put the four new tiers on top of the vanilla levels. In 1.0 the Cultivator already has quality 1-3 (Bronze and Corewood at the Forge) and the Forge of Potential refines it past 3 with a Wooden Battle Idol (wiki), so the tiers are quality 4-7 (raise m_maxQuality to 7): black metal 4, eitr 5, flametal 6, bloodgold 7. Add the tier materials to the Cultivator recipe with m_amount 0, so they never block recipe discovery or the first craft, and let a Piece.Requirement.GetAmount postfix (on those requirement objects only) return each level's list: BlackMetal 5 + LinenThread 10, Eitr 15, FlametalNew 5, Gold ('Bloodgold') 5, and 0 for the vanilla Bronze and Corewood above level 3. A 0 amount hides the row and is skipped by the checks. Remove the idol (m_upgraderResource) requirement so the Forge of Potential skips the Cultivator and cannot push it into a tier, and record the tier in m_customData in an InventoryGui.DoCrafting postfix (the upgrade creates a new item with empty custom data), so a cultivator refined past 3 before install does not count. The vanilla upgrade unequips and replaces the old cultivator and keeps m_name $item_cultivator, so PlantEasily and PlantEverything still recognise it. Replant action (local player, cultivator equipped): the Use key, read in a Player.UpdatePlacement postfix; it is free because Player.UpdateHover clears m_hovering in place mode. On gamepad, JoyUse in the Alternative layouts; in the Default layout JoyUse toggles the piece menu, so use the Remove button there, caught in a Player.UpdatePlacement prefix that calls ZInput.ResetButtonStatus, so neither vanilla removal nor PlantEverything's removal also fires. Raycast from the camera with m_interactMask (the mask Player.FindHoverObject uses) within m_maxInteractDistance, and look for a Pickable or TreeBase whose prefab name is in the tier table and whose tier is at most the cultivator's. Check Location.IsInsideNoBuildLocation, PrivateArea.CheckAccess, stamina and durability as the vanilla remove path does, claim the ZDO, harvest any fruit with Pickable.Interact, destroy the plant with ZNetScene.Destroy (unless the pick already destroyed it), and give one transplant item (dropped if the inventory is full). A Hud.UpdateCrosshair postfix shows '[E] Replant <plant>' or the tier needed. Each transplant item plants a cloned sapling on _CultivatorPieceTable whose only m_grownPrefabs entry is the vanilla plant, so grown plants are vanilla prefabs; clear Piece.m_cultivatedGroundOnly and Plant.m_needCultivatedGround. Fiddlehead and smoke puff saplings get Plant.m_biome and Piece.m_onlyInBiome = AshLands plus m_tolerateHeat. Lingonberry gets DeepNorth plus m_tolerateCold and Piece.m_allowedInDeepSnow. The Yggdrasil sapling (from YggaShoot_small1 or YggaShoot1-3) grows into YggaShoot1-3. It uses Piece.m_mustConnectTo = YggdrasilRoot with a configurable m_connectRadius, and a Plant.Grow prefix lets a Healthy sapling grow only when ResourceRoot.Drain(cost) on a cached nearby root succeeds (a Plant.GetHoverText postfix explains the wait). A Plant.Grow postfix sets a grown bush to picked, so replanting never creates fruit. Replanted one-shot forage gets a respawn cycle from a Pickable.Awake prefix keyed on a custom ZDO flag; the first grown instance is set up in the Plant.Grow postfix, which must also start UpdateRespawn because its Awake already ran.
ideas.risks: The vanilla Cultivator already has three bronze levels and Forge of Potential refinement (wiki; recipe values not checked in game data), so the tier plan changes vanilla: the Cultivator can no longer be refined, a player must reach bronze level 3 before black metal, and quality 7 needs a level-7 station by Recipe.GetRequiredStationLevel unless Player.RequiredCraftingStation is patched per tier. The literal alternative (separate cultivator items, as the sheet words it) needs its own m_name per item, because Inventory.RemoveItem, CountItems and ObjectDB.GetRecipe match by name; a cultivator consumed as an ingredient is not unequipped (Inventory.RemoveItem does not unequip); and PlantEasily's grid and PlantEverything's cultivator removal only work when m_name is $item_cultivator. Quality tiers keep one icon and model; a per-tier icon means patching the one-line ItemDrop.ItemData.GetIcon (inlining risk). Mushrooms, thistle, dandelion, fiddlehead and smoke puff look one-shot in vanilla. PlantEverything writes respawn times into these prefabs but adds m_hideWhenPicked only to Pickable_Stone, which suggests the vanilla forage already hides a child when picked (a picked wild mushroom would then stay as a hidden, picked ZDO instead of being destroyed). Either way a replanted copy gives one harvest without our respawn fix; dump the prefabs to confirm. Transplant items and saplings are unknown prefabs for players without the mod and after an uninstall: the items are dropped from inventories and unfinished saplings stay invisible in the save until the mod is back; grown plants are vanilla prefabs and survive. Wild vegetation is placed once per zone (ZoneSystem.SpawnZone), so uprooting is a permanent move; it needs the ward check. Two players uprooting the same plant in the same instant could both get an item (same race as the hammer). Yggdrasil: Plant.HaveGrowSpace fails on any non-plant collider within m_growRadius and Plant.HaveRoof on anything overhead, so m_connectRadius must be larger than m_growRadius and an overhanging root may block growth. CanDrain is level > cost, so the cost must stay below m_maxLevel (C# default 100). Roots regenerate (C# default 1 per second), so a one-off drain is cheap. CanDrain reads a possibly stale ZDO copy on non-owners. Plant.SUpdate calls Grow on every pass once the grow time is over, so the prefix must be cheap and drain only a Healthy sapling. PlantEverything adds a Piece to the vanilla pickable prefabs and replaces Player.RemovePiece while the cultivator is held: the Remove button deletes any flora it manages, wild bushes and forage included (fruit harvested first, no refund by default). So 'has a Piece' cannot tell wild from planted, the Remove button is taken, and its produce-paid bushes undercut the transplant items. Unverified (prefab): the cultivator table's m_canRemovePieces, the idol requirement on the Cultivator recipe, whether the YggaShoot prefabs carry TreeBase (the wiki calls the Yggdrasil shoot a choppable tree), and which layers the forage colliders use.

ideas.inspiration: Planting wild flora is solved: PlantEverything (and now RestlessPlant) lets the cultivator plant every plant on this list, PlantEverything even a Sap-paid Yggdrasil sapling. But they create new plants from produce, so a wild bush is never worth moving, and nothing is gated by progression. PlantEverything's and Groundwork's cultivators can already delete wild pickables but return no plant. Balrond's and ZethProj's higher-tier cultivators are only better tools. Borrow PlantEverything's per-biome m_tolerateHeat / m_tolerateCold flags and its respawn times for one-shot forage (ideas only, it is GPL), and Groundwork's prefab allowlist with vanilla distance, ward and ownership checks. Ours would differ in four ways. Transplanting moves a finite wild plant, because vegetation never regrows once removed, so scouting the map for good bushes matters. Each biome's flora is gated by the matching cultivator tier. The Yggdrasil sapling ties farming to the Mistlands Ancient Roots (the sap collector's reservoir) instead of a flat cost. ideas.name: Combat pet
ideas.description: Animal handling skill that allows you to train tamed animals and bring them in combat with you, Training and fighting with them makes them gain XP, increasing their stats (up to 5 stars). Every star they gain, they gain a new skill to use in combat, Naturally spawned starred animals already have the abilities
ideas.sketch: Stars are the vanilla creature level (ZDO level, 1 = no star, 6 = 5 stars). Character.SetLevel has no owner check, so the mod calls it on the pet's ZDO owner; it rescales max HP (Character.SetupMaxHealth = base x level), and damage follows the level through Attack.GetLevelDamageFactor (1 + 0.5 per extra level). Wild animals keep their spawn level when tamed, so abilities keyed on GetLevel() give natural 1-2 star animals their abilities for free. Pet XP is a custom ZDO float written only by the pet's owner. It comes from three sources: a Character.RaiseSkill postfix (a tame's own hits call it); a kill bonus from a Character.OnDeath postfix, sent to the pet's owner through an RPC registered in Tameable.Awake; and reduced, capped XP for sparring with training dummies (BaseAI.IsEnemy already makes dummies enemies of tames). A new Animal Handling skill (Jotunn SkillManager, or patches on Skills.IsSkillValid and Skills.GetSkillDef) rises on the handler's own client through an RPC. It gates the star cap and adds damage through the vanilla ZDO float RandomSkillFactor, which Character.GetRandomSkillFactor multiplies into the melee, area and projectile hits (Attack) of a non-player character. Active abilities are cloned attack items added in a Humanoid.GiveDefaultItems postfix, and added directly on level-up. Humanoid.EquipBestWeapon, called about once a second while the pet has a target, picks them by range, interval and AiTarget, and they reuse each animal's own attacks (wolf, boar, lox, asksvin, moose). Passive abilities are status effects that the owner re-applies. Patches on EnemyHud.ShowHud/UpdateHuds and LevelEffects.SetupLevelVisualization show stars 3-5. The mod sets m_commandable in ZNetScene.Awake on every combat species whose prefab lacks it, and a Procreation.Procreate patch clamps offspring (newborns and eggs) to the natural maximum level.
ideas.risks: Non-owner clients read Character.m_level from the ZDO only in Character.Awake. A mid-session star-up must therefore be broadcast (RPC or ZDO poll), and vanilla clients keep the old level until the pet reloads. That includes its damage if a vanilla client takes ownership. The pet's AI owner is not necessarily its handler, and kills resolve on the victim's owner, so every XP path needs an RPC (BetterTames silently skips that case). Custom skills are dropped on load when the mod is removed (Skills.IsSkillValid). Vanilla scaling at 5 stars is 6x HP and 3.5x damage, and flattening it only works where the pet's owner has the mod. The RandomSkillFactor bonus does not reach AoE payloads (a non-player Aoe ignores it). Support (FriendHurt) abilities are only picked while the pet has an enemy target. Death stays permanent (Tameable.OnDeath only drops the saddle). About 25 abilities (5 stars x wolf, boar, lox, asksvin, moose) need balancing and must use animation triggers each Animator already has. The hen has no attack-like asset, so it probably cannot fight. Which vanilla tames are commandable is prefab data, and sources disagree about lox. Conflicts: StarLevelSystem/CLLC/ReefLevels (level scaling and star UI), BetterTames and Monster Level Up (their own kill level-ups), BetterTames, GrindstoneSkills, ReefLevels and our Breeding revamp (offspring stars), and BeastMaster/AllTameable/LetMeTameYou (Tameable patches).

ValBall and BeastMaster grow hidden stat multipliers instead of stars (BeastMaster's 10 training levels are explicitly not stars), so other players cannot see the progress. GrindstoneSkills and BeastMaster's Taming Mastery show that a player skill can carry pet bonuses. ReefLevels already draws up to five stars in the nameplate. Borrow: ValBall's XP weighting by biome, victim stars and bosses; TrollCompanion's visible thresholds and shared kill credit; BeastMaster's 'training while fed and near the owner'; WolfPack's attack-the-hovered-target command; Cartur's m_commandable switch. Ours differs in these ways. The stars are the vanilla creature level, which is visible, synced, already scales HP and damage, and means natural 1-2 star animals arrive with their abilities. Each species (including the Deep North moose) gets one ability per star, built from its own attacks. XP is routed to the pet's ZDO owner by RPC. A handler skill gates the star cap and adds damage through the vanilla RandomSkillFactor. Star UI goes up to 5 stars. Offspring are clamped, so breeding cannot copy trained stars. When StarLevelSystem or ReefLevels is installed, leave star display to it rather than drawing a second set.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] VMods.Core content registration helpers (prefab clone + register)
infrastructure.sketch: A shared library API (RegisterItem/Piece/Recipe/StatusEffect/Prefab) that clones vanilla prefabs under an inactive DontDestroyOnLoad root and validates names (no spaces or parentheses, unique hash). It de-duplicates SharedData on clones and injects content idempotently into ZNetScene (Awake prefix) and both ObjectDBs (Awake/CopyOtherDB postfix + UpdateRegisters). This is essentially a minimal in-house Jotunn; alternatively adopt Jotunn itself.
infrastructure.risks: Duplicate names throw inside vanilla Awake and can break world load. Items unregistered at Player.Load are permanently deleted. Prefab edits persist across sessions (idempotency). The SharedData sharing semantics need a runtime check.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Mod version handshake (mod parity check)
infrastructure.sketch: Register a peer RPC in an OnNewConnection postfix. The client sends {guid, version, required} for every VMods plugin. The server validates in an RPC_PeerInfo prefix and rejects with Error(3) plus a readable reason sent first via RemotePrint or a custom RPC. The client mirrors the check against the server's list. Per-mod policy: required, optional, or client-only.
infrastructure.risks: Must not block vanilla-compatible client-only mods. Message ordering relies on the reliable channel. Crossplay console players are excluded from required-mod servers.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Server-authoritative config sync
infrastructure.sketch: Mark config entries as server-synced. On peer ready, the server pushes a compressed ZPackage of values; on change, it re-broadcasts. Clients override their local values while connected and restore them on disconnect. Could wrap the ServerSync library instead of writing our own.
infrastructure.risks: Payload size on PlayFab relay. Admin-only edits need a socket-identity check (routed-RPC sender is spoofable). Values must be applied before owners use them.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Localization loader
infrastructure.sketch: Each mod ships translations/<Language>.json (or yaml) embedded. The core adds words in a SetupLanguage postfix with English fallback, and also immediately if the Localization instance already exists. It enforces the $vm_<mod>_ token prefix.
infrastructure.risks: The LRU cache keeps [token] placeholders if a token is used before registration. Tokens must be sent over the network instead of localized text.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Console command framework + live tuning knobs
infrastructure.sketch: Register a 'vm <mod> <sub>' command tree in an InitTerminal postfix, with isCheat:false for diagnostics (status, dump ZDO keys, list registered content) and remoteCommand for admin server actions. A dev-build helper reads Terminal.TryTest* for live tuning.
infrastructure.risks: isCheat:true permanently flags characters as cheated. Cheat commands only run on the host or server.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Input helper with vanilla-consistent gating
infrastructure.sketch: VmInput.CanTakeInput() mirrors Player.TakeInput's UI checks. KeyboardShortcut config entries are evaluated via ZInput.GetKey/GetKeyDown, with optional gamepad chords via ZInput Joy* buttons.
infrastructure.risks: Real rebindable actions in the settings UI would need reflection into ZInput.m_buttons and are deferred to UX.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Network/persistence helpers (keys, owner RPC, session hashes)
infrastructure.sketch: A typed key registry (static readonly int hashes with a vm.<mod>. prefix), per-session re-registration of session-only keys (server included), a RequestOwner/Apply-on-owner RPC pattern helper modeled on Container, and typed m_customData accessors (bool, int, float, compact json) with namespaced keys.
infrastructure.risks: Writing ZDOs as non-owner gets overwritten. m_customData is lost when stackable items merge. Keep payloads small (whole-ZDO resend).

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Custom SoftRef asset injection (locations / dungeon rooms)
infrastructure.sketch: Generate an AssetID for mod prefabs and register an AssetLoader entry in AssetBundleLoader.Instance via reflection (Jotunn-style), then add ZoneLocation entries through a LocationList instance or a SetupLocations postfix. Only needed when Exploration features add locations or rooms.
infrastructure.risks: Relies on internal loader structures that can change per patch. Location placement is generated server-side in ghost zones, so the server must have the mod. World-gen changes are permanent in saves.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Runtime self-tests & topology test scripts
infrastructure.sketch: A 'vm selftest' command asserts engine assumptions after spawn: SharedData reference sharing, registration round-trip, customData survival through drop/pickup/container, session hashes present. Scripts launch the local dedicated server (-nographics -batchmode) and two clients for single-player, host, and dedicated test matrices.
infrastructure.risks: The local dedicated server is 1.0.15 vs client 1.0.16 (both network 40). Keep them in sync for release validation.

infrastructure.name: [Infra] Game.isModded policy
infrastructure.sketch: The core plugin sets Game.isModded = true in Awake, as IronGate requests, and documents the consequence in user-facing READMEs.
infrastructure.risks: It disables achievements and achievement stats for users. This is a product decision the user must confirm.

notableMods.why: MIT library, v2.30.2 released 2026-09-21 for 1.0. The standard toolkit for items, pieces, GUI and input, used by several mods in this survey. Read it even if we decide not to depend on it.

notableMods.why: MIT, rebuilt for 1.0 on 2026-09-12, about 940K downloads. Mature reference for inventory and container manipulation, favourites and multiplayer-safe container access.

notableMods.why: Unlicense, pushed 2026-09-28. Best open-source example of minion AI, command keys, worker behaviours and custom pieces with Jötunn. Relevant to summons and rituals.

notableMods.why: LGPL-3.0. Minimal, clean patches of the vanilla ping pipeline (Chat and Minimap), maintained across every update up to Deep North.

notableMods.name: Goldenrevolver mini-mods / QuickStackStore
notableMods.why: Tiny, idiomatic Harmony patches, such as restyling an existing shield by using it on a station. Good minimal-surface examples.

notableMods.name: Jewelcrafting + blaxxun libraries (ItemManager/PieceManager/ServerSync)
notableMods.why: Socket and gem design, and the most widely embedded helper libraries. Also a cautionary tale: embedded old ServerSync broke on 1.0 (ZRoutedRpc.Everybody became a const) and the mod ended up deprecated. Compile against current game assemblies and do not vendor stale binaries.

systems.name: Attacks (melee / area / projectile / chains / secondary)
systems.summary: Attack is a serializable template on SharedData.m_attack/m_secondaryAttack, cloned per swing in Humanoid.StartAttack. Attack.Start gates on reload/stamina/eitr/ammo and sets animator triggers (chains: name+level, 0.2 s window, CharacterAnimEvent.Chain). The animation event Hit/OnAttackTrigger calls Attack.OnAttackTrigger, which consumes ammo and dispatches to DoMeleeAttack (4-degree ray fan, multi-hit damage split, last chain x2), DoAreaAttack, FireProjectileBurst or DoNonAttack, then calls ResetLoadedWeapon for reload weapons. Costs are reduced by 33% x skill. Damage = GetDamage x random skill factor x multipliers x SEMan.ModifyAttack. Everything runs on the attacker's client. Good hooks: Humanoid.StartAttack, Attack.OnAttackTrigger, Attack.ModifyDamage.

systems.name: Damage pipeline & HitData
systems.summary: Character.Damage runs on the attacker and sends RPC_Damage to the victim's ZDO owner. There, in order: forced stagger, dodge i-frames, PvP gate, difficulty scaling, SEMan.OnDamaged (shields), backstab (unalerted victim, 300 s per-victim cooldown), x2 on staggered monsters, BlockAttack if blockable, pushback, status effect, resistances, armor (ApplyArmor formula), ApplyDamage (ZDO health, stagger accumulation), then DoT SEs. Kill credit uses the ZDO keys Attackers and Modifiers.

systems.name: Blocking, parry, stagger, dodge, stamina/eitr
systems.summary: Humanoid.BlockAttack only blocks frontal hits. A parry needs m_timedBlockBonus > 1 and block held for less than 0.25 s. Block power = base x (1 + 0.5 x Blocking skill) and works like armor. Stamina cost = 25 x blocked/power, adjusted by equipment and SEs. The residual stagger decides whether the block holds. Blocks give 2 adrenaline, parries 5, and a parry staggers the attacker. Stagger threshold = maxHP x m_staggerDamageFactor, decaying at threshold/5 per second. Dodge costs stamina scaled by skill, has i-frames until the DodgeMortal event, is synced through ZDO dodginv, and a perfect dodge (RPC_HitWhileDodging) refunds stamina and gives 10 adrenaline. Stamina and eitr regen are in Player.UpdateStats. The UseEitr RPC is never registered, so remote eitr drain is ignored.

systems.name: Weapon & shield data (SharedData)
systems.summary: SharedData is global per prefab and holds damages, attacks, block fields (m_blockPower, m_timedBlockBonus, m_deflectionForce, block charges), adrenaline fields (m_maxAdrenaline, m_fullAdrenalineSE, block/parry adrenaline), stat modifiers that Player.UpdateModifiers sums via reflection, equip/set SEs, and AI usage fields. Per-item state includes m_customData, which is persisted in inventories, containers and ground drops (ItemDrop.SaveToZDO byte array, version 109) and ignored by vanilla. Vanilla tower shields: ShieldWood/Bone/Iron/Blackmetal/Flametal/GoldTower.

systems.name: Weapon loading (crossbows)
systems.summary: Player.UpdateWeaponLoading, called from PlayerAttackInput, queues a Reload MinorActionData whenever m_weaponLoaded != the current weapon. Duration is Lerp(reloadTime, reloadTime/2, skill). On completion Player.SetWeaponLoaded stores an in-memory ItemData reference and writes the ZDO bool WeaponLoaded, which remote clients and WeaponLoadState use for the visual. Firing (Attack.OnAttackTrigger), any weapon unequip (Humanoid.UnequipItem), HideHandItems (R, swimming), and load or death all reset it. Nothing is persisted. ClearActionQueue cancels an in-progress reload. Non-player Humanoids can never be loaded.

systems.name: Skills
systems.summary: Next-level requirement = floor(level+1)^1.5 x 0.5 + 0.5, with gain = step x factor x m_skillGainRate and a cap of 100. Death lowers all skills by 25% x rate. Player.RaiseSkill applies SE multipliers. Tamed creatures forward XP to their owner's m_levelUpOwnerSkill, which is how summons train Blood Magic. Combat XP comes from melee hits (x1.5 when a character is hit), projectile and AoE hits, blocking (1, or 2 on parry), dodges, sneaking (1/s in stealth range), and archery targets. Skills are purely local and saved in the profile.

systems.name: Sneak, stealth & perception
systems.summary: Player.UpdateStealth computes a crouch stealth factor, Lerp(0.5+0.5L, 0.2+0.4L, sneak), ramps it at 0.25/s and syncs it via ZDO Stealth. Noise (run 30 / walk 15 / jump 30 / dodge 5 / attack 10 and 30 / projectile impact) decays at 4 m/s and syncs via ZDO noise. BaseAI.CanSeeTarget uses viewRange x stealth, a view-angle check only when unalerted, line-of-sight raycasts and mist. MonsterAI becomes alerted when in sight within alertRange x stealth, when damaged, or on nearby projectile hits. A backstab needs an unalerted victim. Sneak XP is 1/s when BaseAI.InStealthRange, else 0.1/s.

systems.name: Adrenaline & trinkets
systems.summary: All changes go through Player.AddAdrenaline, owner-only: gain curves, Game.m_adrenalineRate and SE modifiers. At max, the m_fullAdrenalineSE of each equipped item is added, adrenaline resets to 0 and plays the pop effect. Tier SEs come from m_adrenalineEffects (AdrenalineRush1-4). Degeneration is in UpdateStats. Capacity = Player.m_maxAdrenaline (prefab value, probably 0) + the sum of equipped m_maxAdrenaline, mostly from the trinket. Sources: melee hit +1 x enemy multiplier, miss -5, projectile +2, block +2, parry +5, unblocked hit -5, stagger enemy +5, perfect dodge +10, guardian power +10. Adrenaline is not saved and is mirrored to ZDO adrenaline. Player.m_dodgeAdrenaline is unused.

systems.name: Forsaken (guardian) powers
systems.summary: ItemStand.Interact triggers the delayed DelayedPowerActivation, which calls Player.SetGuardianPower. Player.StartGuardianPower checks gating and cooldown and triggers the gpower animation, whose event calls ActivateGuardianPower. That adds the GP SE by hash to all players within 10 m (RPC_AddStatusEffect for remote players), gives +10 adrenaline and sets the cooldown from SE.m_cooldown. The cooldown ticks in UpdateGuardianPower. Name and cooldown are saved in the profile. Assets: GP_Eikthyr, GP_TheElder, GP_Bonemass, GP_Moder, GP_Yagluth, GP_Queen, GP_Fader.

systems.name: Status effects
